newsitem.title: USA: Police among 11 charged in U.S. drug ring bust.
newsitem.headline: Police among 11 charged in U.S. drug ring bust.

text.p: Four suburban police officers were among 11 individuals charged in federal court Friday with participating in a scheme to distribute cocaine in the Detroit area.

U.S. Attorney Saul Green announced the charges at a news conference Friday and said 10 of the individuals had been arrested and were in custody. The defendants are alleged to be connected to a drug-trafficking organisation in Chicago known as Medina.

As late as this week, the police officers, who included the deputy chief of police in tiny Royal Oak Township, Michigan, were alleged to be involved in providing a location for storage of cocaine being shipped to Detroit.

"The individuals who were identified as police officers were basically acting as security guards for shipments of cocaine to Detroit," said Sandy Palazzolo, a spokeswoman for the U.S. Attorney's office in Detroit.

The charges included conspiracy to possess more than five kgs of cocaine with intent to distribute and distibution of more than five kgs of cocaine. They each face sentences of 10 years to life in prison and/or fines of up to $4 million.
